newsitem.title: USA: Stuck shuttle door holds up U.S. space walk.
newsitem.headline: Stuck shuttle door holds up U.S. space walk.

text.p: A stuck airlock hatch was preventing two astronauts from leaving the shuttle Columbia on Thursday to begin a space walk and practice assembly of NASA's planned international space station.

Astronauts Tammy Jernigan and Tom Jones were supposed to open the hatch leading to the shuttle's cargo bay at about 9:20 p.m. EST (0220 GMT) but could not fully turn the handle that unlatches the 40-inch (101 cm) diameter door

"We're having a hard time opening the outer hatch," veteran astronaut Story Musgrave informed mission control as Jernigan and Jones, wearing bulky space suits, struggled with the door in the shuttle's cramped airlock.
"The handle rotates about 30 degrees and then it doesn't seem to want to move," Jernigan said.
Flight controllers at mission control in Houston huddled around their desks to discuss the problem. They recommended the astronauts put more force on the handle but it still refused to budge.
The next step would be to pressurize and then depressurize the airlock compartment slightly in the hope a change in air pressure would free the door, NASA spokesman Rob Navias said.
The astronauts were due to make a 6 1/2-hour spacewalk to practice assembly of the international space station, the first component of which is scheduled for launch in November 1997.
